source.name: Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC)
source.document: MERC Order in Case No. 75 of 2025 dated 25 March 2026 (MSEDCL review of MYT Order, post remand proceedings), published on MSEDCL's tariff details page
source.table: Summary of LT Tariff for FY 2026-27, effective from 1 April, 2026
source.section: Revised category-wise Tariffs - LT Residential, LT I(B)
source.excerpt: LT I(B): LT - Residential, Rs/conn/mth: Fixed 130 for each slab; 1-100 units: energy 3.96, wheeling 1.60; 101-300 units: 10.80, 1.60; 301-500 units: 15.03, 1.60; Above 500 units: 17.53, 1.60; Three Phase Charges 435.

verification_notes: Controlling order: the 25-03-2026 post-remand order in Case 75 of 2025. The 28-03-2025 MYT order (Case 217 of 2024) was stayed, the 25-06-2025 review order was set aside by the Bombay High Court on 3-11-2025 and remanded by the Supreme Court; para 26.5-26.8 (pages 88-89) confirm the tariff in force from 1 July 2025 and that the FY 2025-26 tariff is unchanged. Cross-check: MERC's 25-06-2025 review order (Case 75 of 2025, https://www.mahadiscom.in/consumer/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Order_Case-No.75-of-2025.pdf) prints identical LT I(B) rows for FY 2025-26 (PDF page 52) and FY 2026-27 (PDF page 53). Billing method: residential consumers are billed on a telescopic tariff (MERC Case 217 of 2024, para 2.4.5, page 62). Energy and wheeling charges are stored separately as printed in the order (the printed FY 2025-26 first-slab total of 5.74 differs by Rs 0.01 from 4.28 + 1.47). Fixed charge is the single-phase Rs/connection/month rate; three-phase connections pay an additional charge (Rs 430 in FY 2025-26, Rs 435 in FY 2026-27) and connection phase is not collected. Electricity duty, FAC and taxes are not modelled. MSEDCL does not serve all of Maharashtra (BEST, AEML-D and TPC-D also distribute in Mumbai), so this schedule only applies when the DISCOM is identified as MSEDCL.
